strings.name: Cyril Ramaphosa
strings.role: President of South Africa · Democratic transition negotiator
strings.summary: Ramaphosa moved from anti-apartheid student activism and mineworker organizing into politics, negotiating for the ANC and chairing the Constitutional Assembly. After a business career, he returned to government, became president in 2018 and led a coalition after the ANC lost its parliamentary majority in 2024. His economic and anticorruption pledges have been scrutinized alongside controversy over Marikana and the Phala Phala cash scandal.
strings.coverageNote: Sources checked through 13 November 2026. Selected milestones do not constitute an exhaustive record of all news or controversies.
strings.influence.rationale: Moved from trade unions and democratic-transition negotiations to South Africa's presidency, participating in economic reform, anti-corruption efforts and African multilateral cooperation.
strings.facts.fact-01.label: Birthplace
strings.facts.fact-02.label: Education
strings.facts.fact-02.value: University of South Africa, BProc law degree (1981)
strings.highlights.highlight-01.title: Negotiation and constitution-making
strings.highlights.highlight-01.text: Led the ANC’s negotiating team and chaired the Constitutional Assembly after 1994.
strings.highlights.highlight-02.title: Transition to coalition government
strings.highlights.highlight-02.text: Won reelection by parliament and formed a multiparty government after the ANC lost its majority in 2024.
strings.timeline.event-01.title: Addressed local election results
strings.timeline.event-01.text: Spoke as president at the electoral commission’s results announcement, emphasizing local governance and public services.
strings.timeline.event-02.title: Phala Phala proceedings paused
strings.timeline.event-02.text: The High Court temporarily halted impeachment proceedings over the farm cash scandal pending judicial review of the preliminary report.
strings.timeline.event-03.title: Reelected after coalition negotiations
strings.timeline.event-03.text: Parliament reelected him after the ANC lost its majority; he subsequently announced a multiparty cabinet.
strings.timeline.event-04.title: Became South Africa’s president
strings.timeline.event-04.text: Took office after Jacob Zuma’s resignation, promising action on corruption and economic reform.
strings.timeline.event-05.title: Marikana inquiry findings released
strings.timeline.event-05.text: He was a mining-company director during the 2012 police killings; the inquiry did not find him to be the cause of the massacre, while accountability remained contested.
strings.timeline.event-06.title: Became deputy president
strings.timeline.event-06.text: Entered Zuma’s government after returning to ANC leadership and became ANC president in 2017.
strings.timeline.event-07.title: Moved into business
strings.timeline.event-07.text: Left parliament after constitution-making and later built an investment business and served on company boards.
strings.timeline.event-08.title: Chaired the Constitutional Assembly
strings.timeline.event-08.text: Entered parliament after the first democratic election and oversaw the drafting process for the new constitution.
strings.timeline.event-09.title: Led the ANC’s negotiating team
strings.timeline.event-09.text: Became ANC secretary-general and participated in multiparty negotiations to end apartheid.
strings.timeline.event-10.title: Helped found the mineworkers’ union
strings.timeline.event-10.text: Founded the National Union of Mineworkers with colleagues and became its first general secretary.
strings.timeline.event-11.title: Completed his law degree
strings.timeline.event-11.text: Continued his studies by correspondence after political detention and earned a UNISA law degree.
strings.timeline.event-12.title: Born in Johannesburg
strings.timeline.event-12.text: Born in Johannesburg; his family was later forcibly relocated to Soweto.
